definition.def: The style of something is the general way in which it is done or presented, which often shows the attitudes of the people involved.
examples: Our children's different needs and learning styles created many problems.
Belmont Park is a broad sweeping track which will suit the European style of running.
Sam celebrated in fine style.

definition.def: If people or places have style, they are smart and elegant.
examples: Bournemouth, you have to admit, has style.
Both love doing things in style.
She had not lost her grace and style.

definition.def: The style of a product is its design.
examples: His 50 years of experience have given him strong convictions about style.
Several styles of hat were available.

definition.def: In the arts, a particular style is characteristic of a particular period or group of people.
examples: ...six scenes in the style of a classical Greek tragedy.
...a mixture of musical styles.
...the revival of the gothic style.

definition.def: If something such as a piece of clothing, a vehicle, or someone's hair is styled in a particular way, it is designed or shaped in that way.
examples: His thick blond hair had just been styled before his trip. [be VERB-ed]
...classically styled clothes. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you say that something is not someone 's style, you mean that it is not the way in which they usually do things, or it is different from the sort of thing they usually like.
examples: The Prime Minister was not off guard. That is not his style.
To be honest, the house is not quite our style.

definition.def: If someone or something cramps your style, their presence or existence restricts your behaviour in some way. [informal]
examples: People think having your dad on tour would cramp your style.

definition.def: If you style out a difficult situation, you behave in a confident way in the hope that no one notices the problem. [informal]
examples: You've styled out this break-up, but don't forget what you've learned.  [VERB PARTICLE noun]
Where the mistake is obvious, the best option is to style it out.  [V it P ]

definition.def: If you style out a particular outfit, you wear it with confidence and style. [informal]
examples: She can style out any look, from blazers to leopard-print trousers.  [VERBPHRASE noun]

definition.def: -style combines with nouns and adjectives to form adjectives which describe the style or characteristics of something.
examples: ...the development of a Western-style political system.
...a hearty country-style dinner.

definition.def: -style combines with adjectives and nouns to form adverbs which describe how something is done.
examples: Guests have been asked to dress 1920s-style.

examples.sentence: The use of an architectural style cannot be said to start or finish on a specific date.
A new style of architecture emerged to reflect more idealistic notions for the future.
By the 1930s many buildings emerging from this movement were designed in the International Style.
By the 1950s, the International Style had developed into a universal approach to building, which standardised the appearance of new buildings in cities across the world.
The architectural style usually referred to as High Tech was also emerging.
Like the Modernists, people today recognise that a well designed environment improves the quality of life but is not necessarily achieved by adopting one well defined style of architecture.
Such visits are made says Boorstin, within the environmental bubble of the familiar American style hotel which insulates the tourist from the strangeness of the host environment.
In many cases, the architectural style of the building further reinforces that notion.
We shouldn't underestimate the importance of the style of a particular artist, their place in history and the artistic environment of their time.
Thus all readers will have the chance to participate in a mathematical experience, to appreciate the beauty of mathematics, and to become familiar with its logical, yet intuitive, style of thinking.
